evals.name: python-native-workflow-store-and-hardcoded-key
evals.prompt: Before we deploy the travel concierge agent in ./travel-concierge-python, check its state store and memory configuration. It's a dapr-agents project.
evals.expected_output: A review-agent-memory report with Language: python. Critical DAG-MEM-001 because resources/agent-workflow.yaml has no actorStateStore: "true"; warning DAG-MEM-003 for the plain-text OpenAI key in resources/llm-provider.yaml; DAG-MEM-006 for the DurableAgent in main.py (no state=AgentStateConfig(...)) is only a Please verify item, because state auto-wires from the agent-workflow component. ConversationListMemory in examples/local_demo.py (marked dev-only, and ineffective because state auto-wires from agent-workflow) is downgraded to Please verify. agent-memory.yaml is correct and not flagged. Retired DAG-MEM-004 and DAG-MEM-005 do not appear.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: python`
Under `## Critical` the report contains [DAG-MEM-001] citing resources/agent-workflow.yaml (any line 1-14) for the missing actorStateStore: "true"
Under `## Warnings` the report contains [DAG-MEM-003] citing resources/llm-provider.yaml:9 or :10 for the hardcoded key, with a Fix that uses `{{OPENAI_API_KEY}}` templating or a secretKeyRef

If the report contains [DAG-MEM-006] for travel-concierge-agent/main.py, it appears under `## Please verify` (state auto-wires from resources/agent-workflow.yaml), NOT under `## Warnings` or `## Critical`

DAG-MEM-002 for ConversationListMemory in travel-concierge-agent/examples/local_demo.py appears under `## Please verify`, NOT under `## Critical`, and its text says the memory is ineffective or overridden because state auto-wires from agent-workflow, or that the file is dev-only

The report does NOT contain DAG-MEM-007 for resources/agent-memory.yaml (actorStateStore is "false"), DAG-MEM-008 (single-agent project, no registry), DAG-MEM-009 (no component has actorStateStore "true"), or the retired ids DAG-MEM-004 and DAG-MEM-005
The report ends with a `## Next steps` section with it is the last section (nothing follows its bullets)

Tool use: the run uses only Read, Grep and Glob to inspect the project — no Bash, PowerShell, Write or Edit call appears in the transcript (the two harness output files written with Write are excluded) — and no fixture file is modified

evals.name: dotnet-sessionless-invoker-and-package-floor
evals.prompt: Our helpdesk agent in helpdesk-dotnet (Microsoft Agent Framework + Diagrid.AI.Microsoft.AgentFramework) forgets everything between /ask calls. Can you review its memory and persistence setup?
evals.expected_output: A review-agent-memory report with Language: dotnet. DAG-MEM-005 for invoker.RunAgentAsync in Program.cs called without an AgentSession and with no CreateSessionAsync/AttachSession anywhere. DAG-MEM-006 for Microsoft.Extensions.AI pinned at 10.1.0 (below 10.6.0). The explicit Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10 reference, the context.RunAgentAsync calls inside TicketWorkflow, and the absence of agent-memory.yaml are not findings.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: dotnet`
The report contains [DAG-MEM-005] citing HelpdeskApp/Program.cs:30 (invoker.RunAgentAsync without a session), with a Fix mentioning CreateSessionAsync and AttachSession
The report contains [DAG-MEM-006] citing HelpdeskApp/HelpdeskApp.csproj:11 for Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.1.0 being below 10.6.0
The report does NOT flag the Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10 reference (HelpdeskApp.csproj:10) under DAG-MEM-006 and does not recommend removing it
The report does NOT cite HelpdeskApp/Workflows/TicketWorkflow.cs for DAG-MEM-005 (the context.RunAgentAsync calls on lines 13 and 17 are one-shot workflow agent runs)

The report does NOT treat the missing resources/agent-memory.yaml as a finding, and contains no DAG-MEM-001 (agent-workflow.yaml has actorStateStore "true") and no DAG-MEM-003 (the key is `{{ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}}`)
The report uses no Python-only rule ids (DAG-MEM-002, DAG-MEM-008)

Tool use: the run uses only Read, Grep and Glob to inspect the project — no Bash, PowerShell, Write or Edit call appears in the transcript (the two harness output files written with Write are excluded) — and no fixture file is modified

evals.name: python-wrapper-unused-memory-helper
evals.prompt: Review the memory setup of our support bot in ./support-bot-wrapper-python. It's an OpenAI Agents SDK agent wrapped with the diagrid package, and it should remember what returning customers said earlier.
evals.expected_output: A review-agent-memory report with Language: python. Warning DAG-MEM-012 because DaprMemoryStore() in support-agent/main.py:20 uses the default store `statestore`, which is not in resources/ (dapr.yaml sets resourcesPath). Info DAG-MEM-011 because the DaprMemoryStore is never read or written (no load_memory/save_memory) and the runner keeps history per workflow instance only, so nothing carries across calls. No DAG-MEM-001 (agent-workflow.yaml has actorStateStore "true"), no native-only rules, no retired ids.
expectations: The report section (after the optional one-line `Reviewing <path>` scope echo) starts with `# Dapr review — review-agent-memory` and contains `Language: python`

Under `## Warnings` the report contains [DAG-MEM-012] citing support-agent/main.py:20 and naming the missing `statestore` component, with a Fix that adds a component to resources/ and/or passes an explicit store_name

Under `## Suggestions` the report contains [DAG-MEM-011] citing support-agent/main.py:20 (or :22 for the runner), and its Why says the store is never used (no load_memory/save_memory calls) or that the runner keeps history per workflow instance / per run only
The report does NOT contain DAG-MEM-001 or DAG-MEM-009 (exactly one component, agent-workflow, has actorStateStore "true"), DAG-MEM-003, or DAG-MEM-008 (no registry, single app)

The report does NOT contain the native-only ids DAG-MEM-002 or DAG-MEM-006, nor the retired ids DAG-MEM-004 or DAG-MEM-005, and does not ask for state=AgentStateConfig(...) or ConversationDaprStateMemory
The report does NOT flag the absence of resources/agent-memory.yaml or of a runner state_store= argument as a finding on its own
The report ends with a `## Next steps` section that suggests review-agent-observability, it is the last section (nothing follows its bullets)

Tool use: the run uses only Read, Grep and Glob to inspect the project — no Bash, PowerShell, Write or Edit call appears in the transcript (the two harness output files written with Write are excluded) — and no fixture file is modified
